L01.text: Tonight, the Moon is gone. The first thing you'd notice isn't the sky. It's the sea.

L02.text: The Moon is the main reason we have tides. Its gravity pulls the ocean into a bulge, and Earth spins underneath it.

L03.text: Without it, only the Sun is left pulling, and the tides shrink to about a third.

L04.text: Rock pools dry up, and the beach gets very boring.

L05.text: Nights get much darker, too. And corals that time their spawning by the full moon would lose their calendar.

L06.text: But the big one is slower. The Moon keeps Earth's tilt steady, wobbling only between about twenty-two and twenty-four and a half degrees.

L07.text: Without it, the tilt could swing wildly, anywhere from nearly zero to eighty-five degrees.

L08.text: Luckily, that would take millions of years. Unluckily, when it happens, the seasons go completely bonkers.

L09.text: So next time you see the Moon, say thanks. It's been holding the planet steady for billions of years.
